the two-dimensional acoustic pattern derived (2DPD) strain parameters closely correlated with the one-dimensional (1D) tissue Doppler (TD) derived strain measurements.
the two-dimensional acoustic pattern derived (APD) strain parameters closely correlate to one-dimensional tissue Dopuler (TDI) derived strain measurements.

two-dimensional acoustic pattern derived longitudinal strain measurements correlate with one-dimensional longitudinal tissue Doppler derived peak systolic and peak early diastolic strain measurements in healthy volunteers.

the development of a novel method for the estimation of strain in the heart.

the use of a novel ultrasound technique, acoustic pattern derived strain imaging, to quantify myocardial strain in a porcine model of ischemic cardiomyopathy and to compare these measurements with conventional one-dimensional tissue Dopplers.

the 2-D pattern derived strain parameters correlate with the 1-D strain measurements.

two-dimensional acoustic pattern derived parameters (strain and strain rate) closely correlate with one dimensional (1D) tissue Doppler derived parameters (strain, strain rate and displacement).

the 2D strain parameters are highly correlated with the conventional TDI strain parameters, and the 2D pattern derived strain parameters have better correlation with the conventional TDT strain parameters compared with the strain rate parameters.
the 2-Dimensional (2-D) acoustic strain pattern is a good surrogate for the 1-Dimensional (1-D) tissue Doppler derived longitudinal strain (ε) measurements in patients with dilated cardiomyopathy.
